questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As a student of Asia Studies with specialization it is crucial to master the Chinese language. The best place to do that is in China.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The language program at Peking University greatly enhanced my Chinese language skills.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find information on general logistics. The language course information would not be available until about 7-9 days into the stay. That was no problem for my stay, the only problem was that my university requested information about these courses much earlier and I could not provide it before this time. The main problem was the fact that there are no available course catalogues for graduate students. Undergraduates a provided with a webside through which they can access information about all undergraduate courses and through which they can register to courses. Information about graduate courses can only be provided by personal request to each faculty to provide information on which courses they offer on the relevant semester. Furthermore the registration procedure is in person and requires a back and forth between the faculty and the office for exchange students to fill out a document and get necessary stamples. The information about this procedure is not informed anywhere. It was through several vigorous requests in person at the office for exchange students that I was finally informed about this procedure for registering for a master level course.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was informed to register at the office for exchange student where I could ask for assistance. I was also instructed by email to join a wechatgroup for exchange students where the staff of the office for exchange students responded to inquiries. Inquiries concerning master courses were not responded to, but all other inquiries were.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was very satisfied except this one problem. Graduate students are offered no information as to how to access information on and register for courses. It took a lot of insistance on my side, and I was rather shocked when the responsible person for exchange students advised me to take undergraduate courses instead of graduate courses. Of course I informed her that I was a masters student, and that my university would only give merit to graduate courses. Still she assured me that the undergraduate courses at Peking University are on a very high academic level and questioned whether it was me personally or my home university that would not accept me taking undergraduate courses instead of graduate courses. I think that it would be productive if this misunderstanding was dealt with between the University of Copenhagen and Peking University. It seems as if the University provides undergraduate students access to registering for undergraduate courses with a certain guarantee that they can attend courses with that aberdabei that it is a lottery whether they get a spot. When it comes to graduate courses exchange students need to get permission from the department and the professor of a given course personally. This procedure is so different from the procedure in Denmark that I think students should be informed beforehand about this procedure, specially since there is no information about the procedure on arrival and since it is only provided after a lot of inquiry.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used the app Anjuke to find a studio in Zhongguancun. I was not able to contact any landlord before I was in China because you need to call them. Maybe you can contact them on wechat. This is how it works: you contact them and they will offer to show you the studio on the same day or the day after. You go to see it and if you like it you pay the deposit at the office right after. The rooms go fast. You have to pay a fee to the middleman that shows you the studio if you choose to take it. Make sure that the price is clear beforehand. Some want very little but some want a months rent. I paid half a rent as a fee. Water and heat is calculated besides the rent but shouldnt be that much. I paid 200 for heat for my whole stay. The price for a studio starts at about 6500.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you find your own place it will be more easy to study. If you are not planning on studying in your room a lot a dormitory is fine. A friend of mine had a room mate that once ordered take out at 1 am on the day that my room mate had an exam. Personally I had 5 courses and would not had been able to study well under such circumstances. If you want rent a room in a shared apartment you should know that a lot of land lords that rent out rooms for shared apartment do not rent out rooms to foreigners.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't stay in a dormitory. Can't say much.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy to register. If you don't have a Chinese bank account yet it is good to bring cash for paying insurance since they don't take foreign cards.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I went to the Xintaiyang Student Center and registered myself, bringing the required documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Alle answers to qustions were provided on the wechat group.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was extremely successful but it took a lot of time and effort to register for my graduate course and I was lucky to make it in time. There is no standard procedure and not much help regards registering for graduate courses. Acquiring course information required biking from faculty to faculty to ask which courses the given faculty provided for the semester. Some would print out course information, some would allow you to take a picture of the courses you were interested in from a print out. Then you had to contact the professor of a course you were interested in and ask if you could attend his course. You would have to find the professors contact details yourself since they were not provided. The official faculty webside in English would not necessarily have the information.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are a graduate student: be ready to walk from faculty to faculty OR hurry and find a Chinese graduate student friend and have him help you access his system. Then you can see which courses are provided and you won't have to visit as many faculties.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were great.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took a philosophy MA course and advanced Chinese language courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The was a lot of writing during the semester and much more homework.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Chinese Reading
Oral Chinese
Advanced Business Chinese
Advanced Classical Chinese
Seminar on Chinese and Western Comparative Philosophy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. Advanced Business Chinese and Advanced Classical Chinese are only for those that are interested in the subject. These two courses require more work than the other Chinese language courses. The exams are also more demanding.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I had imagined. It is not expensive but in my neighborhood Zhongguancun it is more expensive than many other areas. If you only eat at the university you can eat for maybe 1800 a month.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were clubs but I didn't have time to attend. However some clubs are not open for foreigners.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were no classical music choirs. Everything else was there. Archery, marsial arts, piano club (for semiprofessionals) etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: calligraphy. Make sure to join in time because you can only join the foreigner club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other cities than Beijing during vacation or prolongued weekend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Everybody is nice and respecful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs or take courses that primarily have chinese students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Traffic. Be careful in traffic. Some bathrooms have no soap.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the traditional culture, the rich food culture, philosophy, tea drinking

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It takes some food work to register for graduate courses but it's worth it
2. be ready for a lot of homework, specially for language courses (if you don't study hard stick with 3 courses, in any case don't take more than 5 courses)
3. Make sure to visit places outside Beijing

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use TAOBAO to buy things in Beijing. Beijing is to big to look for things, and taobao is cheaper. I got blanket, pillow, table etc in Taobao.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my Chinese language skills and deepening my undertsnading of Chinese philosophy.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Registering for courses. Preparing for exam for 5 courses without 'reading vacation.' You have courses right up until exam. Midterm exams are hard. The last exams are even harder.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
